evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We send SMS to about 9,000 smallholder maize farmers in Bungoma and Kakamega counties in Western Kenya, reminding them to apply top-dressing fertilizer in the three weeks after emergence. Interviews confirmed the barrier: they know the window but miss it. Our working draft, sent in Kiswahili from the county extension office, says: 'Apply your top-dressing this week to protect your harvest. Visit your agrovet by Friday.' Our comms lead wants to change it to 'If you miss top-dressing this week you will lose up to a third of your harvest', because losses hit harder. No money is involved. Messages go per phone number, so we can randomize. Which frame should we use?
evals.expected_output: A decision on gain or loss wording in the output template that keeps the gain version as the default and sets aside "losses hit harder" as a reason.
assertions: Records the behavior as one that lowers a risk, with the reason, and says "losses hit harder" is not a reason to use the loss version.
Gives both versions with the same facts, action, sender, and length.
The loss version does not state a harm the gain version does not imply, and "up to a third of your harvest" is removed or flagged as an added claim.
Sets a pre-test with five to ten farmers and a rule for dropping the loss version.
Promises no difference between the two versions.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Should our messages use loss framing? Everyone says loss aversion is stronger.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the draft, the behavior, and whether money is involved, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the draft message or offer and the behavior it asks for.
Asks whether the behavior lowers a risk or reveals one.
Asks whether a loss version would take back or withhold money.
Does not recommend a frame.
Does not write any message text.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our program in Zambia pays community health agents a monthly stipend top-up of ZMW 300 if they complete 40 household visits. Our finance lead proposes paying the full ZMW 300 at the start of the month and deducting ZMW 7.50 for every visit short of 40, so agents feel each missed visit as a loss. Visits are counted from the supervisor's register. Can you set this up as a loss contract?
evals.expected_output: The skill keeps payment on completion as the version to use, does not design the deduction scheme, and names a labor-law or ethics reviewer.
assertions: Says the loss version would take back money agents treat as theirs.
Does not write the terms of the up-front payment with deductions.
Names a labor-law or ethics reviewer as the specialist, before any pilot.
Says what to bring to that reviewer.
Says field studies of loss-framed pay found little effect, and gives no promised gain.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We have decided on a gain frame for the SMS inviting men in Lagos to collect a free HIV self-test kit from the pharmacy. Please write the message in Yoruba and English with the pickup location and opening hours.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the frame is already chosen and the request is for the message itself, and points to the skill that writes it.
assertions: Says the frame is decided, so there is nothing for this skill to choose.
Names draft-lever-content.
Does not write the message.
Does not fill the output template.
